newsitem.title: UK: Dixons drops further amid cautious comment.
newsitem.headline: Dixons drops further amid cautious comment.

text.p: Shares in Dixons Group Plc fell to a five-month low on Thursday, extending yesterday's losses amid cautious comment on the electrical retailer's first half results.
The stock was down 10p at 501 by 0812 GMT, its lowest level since August last year.

Dixons on Wednesday posted a 53 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 57.5 million stg in the first half, at the top end of analyst forecasts but not enough to prevent a wave of profit-taking in the stock which rose sharply through 1996.
The Financial Times influential Lex column said the good news of rising consumer spending was already discounted in Dixons' share price and identified a series of concerns for the stock.
It said the company was struggling to make further market share gains in so-called brown and white goods like cookers and fridges.

Another concern was over a rising tax bill following the government's decision to raise the tax on warranties which generate much of Dixons' profits. Finally it said retail sales growth might slow this year as interest rates rise.
